reuse.why: All six provider link handlers, including the new Fintegra one, go through the new linkBankSyncAccount and assertBankAccountNotLinked; the takeover path copies unlinkAccount's field clearing instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: The five copies of upgrade-or-create/sync/notify are collapsed into one helper, but the helper itself carries two near-identical syncAccount calls behind includeFileId, the unlink field-clearing block is copied from unlinkAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions is a copy of the Enable Banking download function.

placement.why: The shared link logic and the link precondition live in accounts/app.ts next to the handlers and the Fintegra download sits with the other providers in sync.ts; mutating the old account inside an 'assert' function mixes a side effect into a check.

scope.why: Changes cover the refactor and the three features; the institution-null comment is copied onto providers that did not have it, a minor unrelated touch.

maintainability.why: One place now owns account creation/upgrade, first sync and the sync-event, with explicit tables and fileId variation; the includeFileId flag and the duplicated unlink fields are small warts.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked in packages/loot-core/src/server/accounts/app.ts clears the old account with its own copy of unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount instead of a shared local-unlink step.

disguised_duplication.where: The copied unlink update and the Fintegra download function are overt copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink; linkBankSyncAccount carries an includeFileId branch duplicating the syncAccount call to preserve the Pluggy argument list; the takeover re-implements unlinkAccount's detachment.
